mcqs.question: What is the core shift in handling a request that genuinely takes 90 seconds, instead of just raising every timeout?
options: Compress the request payload so it transmits faster
Move the entire endpoint to a faster server instance
Accept the request immediately with a reference, and let the caller check back or be notified later instead of waiting on an open connection
Split the 90-second work into exactly two 45-second calls
mcqs.explanation: The fix is architectural — stop holding a connection open for the full duration and instead return a reference immediately, letting the caller check back. Compression, a faster instance, or splitting into two calls don't address the fundamental mismatch between a synchronous call and genuinely long work.

mcqs.question: A report endpoint now takes 90 seconds instead of 2. Kept synchronous, why does the client end up generating the report twice?
options: The server always runs every report request exactly twice for accuracy
The client's own HTTP timeout (e.g. 30 seconds) fires before the server finishes, so the client retries a request that was actually still succeeding
The database automatically duplicates any query that runs longer than 60 seconds
Report generation is inherently non-deterministic and must be run twice to confirm results
mcqs.explanation: The client's timeout is unrelated to whether the server-side work is healthy, so it fires and triggers a retry even though the original request was still progressing normally — that duplicate work is the actual bug. There's no automatic server-side duplication, no database timeout behavior like that, and report generation being deterministic isn't the issue here.

mcqs.question: What real cost does an async job pattern (accept-and-poll or webhook) add compared to a simple synchronous call?
options: It requires switching the entire API from REST to gRPC
It removes the need for any authentication on the endpoint
It always increases the total wall-clock time the underlying work takes to complete
It needs a job store, a status API, and idempotent job creation to handle retried job-creation requests safely
mcqs.explanation: Async patterns add real infrastructure — tracking job state, exposing status, and making job creation safe to retry — that a synchronous call didn't need. It doesn't require any particular API style, doesn't remove authentication, and doesn't change how long the underlying work itself takes.

mcqs.question: A long-running job fails halfway through. What should the status endpoint and job design support?
options: A single generic "failed" status with no further detail, to keep the API simple
Automatically deleting the job record so the client must resubmit from scratch every time
A status distinguishing retryable from terminal failure, plus enough checkpoint state to resume from where it left off if the work is resumable
Silently retrying the job server-side up to 3 times with no client visibility
mcqs.explanation: Distinguishing retryable from terminal failure tells the client whether retrying is worthwhile at all, and checkpoint state lets a retry skip already-completed work instead of restarting from zero. A single generic status hides useful information, deleting the record forces wasteful full restarts, and silent server-side retries hide failures the client may need to know about.
